sources.description: October 29, 2025 - In Humphreys County, about 42% of residents receive SNAP benefits. In Sharkey, Coahoma, and Claiborne counties, that represents about a third of their residents. Mississippi leads the nation in food assistance reliance.
sources.label: WLBT — Analysis: In Some Miss. Counties, One in Three Residents Needs SNAP Benefits

sources.description: December 23, 2025 - Stricter work requirements for food stamps went into effect in November, putting 33,000 Mississippians at risk of losing their benefits, according to the Center for Budget and Policy Priorities.
sources.label: Mississippi Today — Mississippians Navigate New SNAP Work Requirements

sources.description: December 22, 2025 - The One Big Beautiful Bill Act passed in July 2025 shifts financial burden to states, increasing administrative costs from 50% to 75% in FY27. Food security programs like SNAP have been primarily funded by the federal government.
sources.label: Southern Poverty Law Center — 2026 Policy Priorities for Mississippi

sources.description: January 20, 2023 - Mississippi had the nation's highest rate of individuals eligible for SNAP benefits in 2020 — nearly 1 in 3.
sources.label: U.S. Census Bureau — Mississippians Eligible for Food Assistance

sources.description: March 31, 2025 - For nearly one in eight Mississippians, 13.1% of residents depend on SNAP, far above the 8.3% national average.
sources.label: Public News Service — Proposed SNAP Cuts Would Hit Mississippi Especially Hard

sources.description: July 2025 - The Senate approved the bill 51-50 on July 1, 2025, with Vice President JD Vance casting the tiebreaking vote. It passed the House 218-214 on July 3, 2025.
sources.label: Wikipedia — One Big Beautiful Bill Act
